conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee. I’ll be helping take care of you during this hospital stay. You came in with nausea and vomiting, right?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, that’s right. It’s been going on for about 10 days. Feels just like my past blockages—tightness and pressure all over, especially upper left and right.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. And you’ve had similar episodes before with your mesenteric fibromatosis. You mentioned the pain didn’t get better with your usual morphine suppository?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No, not really. I took it, but the pain stayed strong. I only vomited once this morning, but the nausea is constant.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay. We’ve started your TPN through your femoral line, and you’ll stay on IV fluids. We’ll hold off on food for now—NPO—to let your gut rest.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s fine. I’ve done this before. But can we do something for the nausea? The IV Phenergan helps a little.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re giving IV Phenergan now, but we’ll also try a rectal suppository later to see if that works better for you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, thanks. My last bowel movement was this morning—loose and pencil-thin, like always during a flare.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, and you’re still passing gas, just less than usual. That’s consistent with your history. We’ve ordered an abdominal X-ray to check for obstruction.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the X-ray won’t show a blockage? Because it feels like one.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The X-ray came back. It shows a nonspecific bowel gas pattern—no clear sign of obstruction. There’s stool and air in the rectum, but nothing blocked higher up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Huh. So why do I feel this way if there’s no blockage?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your pain and nausea are likely due to your chronic motility issues and fibromatosis flare. Even without a physical blockage, your gut can act like it’s obstructed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Ah, okay. So we treat it like past flares?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. We’ll continue IV fluids, use IV Dilaudid for breakthrough pain, and keep the morphine suppositories. We’ll also add glycerin suppositories to help move things along.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. How’s the nausea today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: A little better. The rectal Phenergan seemed stronger than the IV. Can I keep using that?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’ll switch to PR Phenergan as needed. We’re also going to try advancing you to clear liquids later if you’re still doing well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Great. I’ve been on TPN for so long, I miss tasting things.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll go slow. If you tolerate clear liquids, we can gradually build up. But if you start vomiting again, we’ll go back to NPO.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve been on clear liquids since yesterday. How’s your stomach holding up?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Pretty good! No vomiting. I’d like to try a soft food—maybe applesauce or broth?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We can add those. But let’s hold off on a full regular diet for now. We don’t want to trigger another episode.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Doctor, I tried a regular meal last night—just mashed potatoes and chicken—and I threw up twice.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I’m sorry to hear that. We’ll switch you back to clear liquids. Your GI doctor agreed—better to go slow. You can start advancing again at home when you’re stable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That makes sense. It’s frustrating, but I don’t want to be back here next week.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll give you a prescription for rectal Phenergan to use at home so you can manage nausea early.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your labs are stable. Hemoglobin is 10.6, which is better than your baseline. No signs of infection.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. And my femoral line—infusions have been burning a bit the last day or two.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I noticed mild redness. We’re going to do a line study tomorrow to check for a leak or tear. You’ll need contrast, so we’ll pre-treat with prednisone since you’ve had reactions before.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, I get hives with iodine. So this is just a scan to check the line, not surgery?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. It’s a fluoroscopy. If there’s a small tear, they can often repair it during the same procedure.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re scheduling the line study for tomorrow morning. You’ll get 50 mg prednisone tonight and again tomorrow, 3 and 1 hour before.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. And my Lupron injection—is it due soon?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You had your last one about three weeks ago, so yes, we’ll give you your monthly Lupron while you’re here.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. I don’t want the fibromatosis to flare more.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The line study is done. There was a small tear near the hub of the red lumen, but they repaired it successfully. No leak in the tunneled part.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So it’s fixed? No replacement needed?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Correct. The catheter itself is intact. We’ll continue using it for TPN. You’ll need to do daily ethanol locks to prevent infection.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I remember—2 mL per lumen, not for IV use. Got it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve been on clear liquids for two days with no vomiting. How’s your pain and nausea?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Much better. Pain is mild, maybe a 3. I’ve been using the morphine suppository once a day.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Great. We’ll keep your pain meds as is. At discharge, we’re increasing the morphine suppository to 20 mg every 6 hours as needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s higher than before. Is that safe?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, it’s within your usual range. You’ve needed more during flares, and we want you to have enough at home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, good. And I’ll keep using the rectal Phenergan as needed?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, 25 mg every 6 hours if nauseated. We’re adding that to your discharge meds.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing really well. We’re planning to discharge you tomorrow morning.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s great! What do I need to do at home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Resume your home TPN through the femoral line. Stay on clear liquids for a few days, then slowly add soft foods as tolerated.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my other meds—everything else stays the same?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, all your regular meds continue—Lupron, levothyroxine, gabapentin, and the rest. We’re just adjusting the pain and nausea meds.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And follow-up with my GI doctor?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, please follow up with Dr. ___ in one week. Call sooner if you have severe pain, vomiting, or redness at the line site.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. I feel a lot better than when I came in.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Your discharge orders are ready. You’re cleared to go home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. I’m ready to get back to my routine.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing well—abdomen soft, pain controlled, no nausea. Keep using the ethanol lock daily on your line.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll do that. And I’ll start advancing my diet slowly, like we talked about.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. Take care, and don’t hesitate to call your team if anything changes.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thanks for everything.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Have a safe trip home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m glad the X-ray didn’t show a blockage. That was worrying me.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, it’s reassuring. Your symptoms were due to your chronic condition, not a new obstruction. That’s why the conservative approach worked.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my migraines—they’ve been okay, just baseline.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we treated them as needed with sumatriptan and butorphanol. No new neuro issues.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. I was worried the pain meds might trigger more headaches.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We monitored that closely. You’re on the same regimen as before, so it shouldn’t be an issue.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my hemoglobin—is it okay that it’s 10.6?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, for you, that’s actually good—better than your usual 25% hematocrit. No need for iron infusion this time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s a relief. I don’t miss those IV treatments.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll keep you on oral ferrous sulfate. Stay consistent with it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. And my constipation—I’ve been using senna and Miralax.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, keep that up. We’re discharging you with both to prevent backup.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve learned—better to stay ahead of it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Smart approach. You know your body best.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: One last thing—my asthma. I used my inhaler a couple times.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we had albuterol available. Your lungs sounded clear. Just keep using it as needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will do. I think that’s everything.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, you’re all set. Discharge paperwork is ready. Take care.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you, Doctor. I appreciate all your help.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re very welcome. Get some rest at home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. And I’ll call if anything comes up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. We’re here if you need us.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thanks again. I’m ready to go.
